section.p: The Quick Brown Fox Tells Story
A typesetting test document for Paragraf Studio
The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. Sphinx of black quartz, judge my vow. Pack my box with five dozen liquor jugs. How vexingly quick daft zebras jump.

Good typography begins with choosing the right typeface for the task. Serif typefaces like Liberation Serif are traditionally used for body text in print because the serifs guide the reader's eye along the baseline, improving reading speed and comprehension across long passages of continuous prose.

Line spacing — the vertical distance between successive baselines — is as important as the typeface itself. A comfortable ratio of line height to font size is typically between 1.4 and 1.6 for body text. Paragraf expresses this as an absolute point value via the lineHeight property.

Justified text is the standard for book and magazine composition. The Knuth–Plass algorithm, used by Paragraf, computes globally optimal line breaks that minimise the total demerits across an entire paragraph, avoiding the ugly rivers of whitespace that simpler greedy algorithms produce. Hyphenation is enabled in this document.

This body-text frame is configured with two columns and a 6 mm gutter. The columns share the available width equally after the gutter is subtracted. Column breaks are handled automatically by the compile layer when text overflows a column's height.

Dimension values throughout studio's template.json accept CSS-like strings: 20mm, 1in, 72pt, or plain numbers for points. The translate layer converts all of these to points before passing them to the compile pipeline.
